The Irish DPC, acting on behalf of the EU, said Google stores users’ location data, violating the GDPR. It also said the data could have been used for targeted advertising or to influence users’ decisions. Google hasn’t had a particularly rewarding 2026, and its legal troubles don’t seem to end. In July 2026, the European Court of Justice held that Google had violated its dominant position by pushing its own services and reserved its previous judgment in the landmark antitrust case, along with a penalty of $4.67 billion . Later that month, the European Commission fined Google close to $1 billion for allegedly violating the Digital Markets Act (DMA). While this was followed by some relief from previously suggested extreme measures in the United States vs. Google lawsuit regarding its monopoly in digital ads, Google has now been hit with another fine of close to half a billion dollars. title: These privacy-focused smart glasses promise not to snoop on you and others
summary: Vonder's new wearable is designed to be glasses first, and an assistant second.
body: Credit: Vonder TL;DR Vonder has announced the launch of its debut collection of smart glasses. These smart glasses come in six frame shapes, three colors, and no camera or display. Pre-orders start on September 28, 2026, with prices starting at $299 and shipping beginning in November. Despite the success of the Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, a stigma hangs over the social media giant’s eyewear. Questions about privacy have been a common theme, not only for those around the user, but also for the user themself. If those concerns are the one thing keeping you away from this genre of wearable, you may be interested to learn about the new smart glasses from Vonder. Founded by the co-founders of XR glasses brand Viture , Vonder is unveiling its debut collection of intelligent eyewear. According to the company, these smart glasses were designed first and foremost to be everyday glasses. As a result, they’re lightweight (under 30g) and made to the wearer’s prescription (from single vision and progressive to Transitions and gradient tint lenses). There are six frames to choose from and three different color options.

title: It’s taken a while, but Adobe Premiere is finally available for Android
summary: A new contestant enters the ring.
body: TL;DR Adobe has finally released the Premiere mobile app on Android, about a year after releasing it for iOS. The video-editing app supports all the functions of its iOS counterpart, including a wide range of templates and several generative AI editing tools. Adobe Premiere for Android is free to download, but requires a device with at least 5GB of RAM and Android 13 (or newer). Video editing program Adobe Premiere has been around for a while, but it took the company until last year to launch a dedicated mobile app. This app was limited to the Apple iPhone, though we recently learned that was about to change. That day is finally here as the Premiere app officially makes its way to Android. Users can now download the Adobe Premiere app for free from the Google Play Store , though certain generative AI features will require a subscription after the free credits expire. In any case, Premiere on Android will offer granular video editing capabilities, along with a trove of other features at no cost.

body: Credit: Stephen Radochia / Android Authority TL;DR Leaker and display enthusiast Ice Universe says that Samsung leads in Privacy Display tech by using four-way baffles to block viewing from the top, bottom, and sides, whereas HUAWEI and Xiaomi only block horizontal views. However, Samsung’s aggressive hardware implementation causes notable off-axis brightness loss, reduced image clarity, and even eye strain and nausea for some users. Competitors like Xiaomi balance privacy with convenience by adding software features such as voice commands, location triggers, and shoulder-surfer detection. body: دفع ثمن قلة مشاركاته مع ريال مدريد كشف تقرير صحفي، اليوم الثلاثاء، عن كواليس استبعاد نجم ريال مدريد، أوريلين تشواميني، من قائمة منتخب فرنسا، التي أعلنها المدرب الجديد، زين الدين زيدان، قبل أيام. وغاب أوريلين تشواميني، عن قائمة زين الدين زيدان للمنتخب الفرنسي، ودفع ثمن قلة مشاركاته مع ريال مدريد. وأوضح مدرب المنتخب الجديد آنذاك: "أوريليين لاعب غائب عن الملاعب منذ شهرين تقريباً، ولم يلعب سوى 120 دقيقة، ولم يبدأ أساسياً إلا مرة واحدة. أعتقد أن من الأفضل له البقاء في مدريد ومواصلة تدريباته من أجل تعافيه". وبحسب صحيفة " ليكيب "، اتصل زين الدين زيدان، بتشواميني قبل إعلان قائمته للاستفسار عن جاهزيته ومعرفة ما إذا كان بإمكانه المشاركة خلال فترة التوقف الدولي الحالية.  وأشار تشواميني إلى عدم جاهزيته البدنية الكاملة بعد إصابته في العضلة الضامة، ولم يرغب زيدان في التسرع. يمكنكم مناقشة الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة وهذا يترك خيارات زيدان بشأن لاعب ريال مدريد مفتوحة على مصراعيها خلال فترة التوقف الدولي في نوفمبر المقبل.

title: Bad news for DIY repairs? Samsung could follow Apple by offering verified batteries.
summary: This will reportedly start with the Galaxy A series phones.
body: Credit: Tushar Mehta / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung will reportedly add a security chip to the batteries in some of its smartphones. This verified battery system could help customers avoid third-party batteries, which might not offer the same safety guarantees. This also comes years after Apple introduced its own battery verification system and parts pairing practice. Apple has long used a verification program for iPhone batteries, allowing you to quickly check if you have a genuine battery in your smartphone. Now, it sounds like Samsung could bring a similar verification system to Galaxy phones. The Elec reports that Samsung will add a security chip to the batteries in some of its phones. The company will apparently add this chip to batteries inside upcoming mid-range phones, including the Galaxy A series.

title: Ozzfest Confirms It Will Return to U.S. in 2027
summary: The event will come to North America for the first time in nearly a decade after previously announcing a show in Birmingham, U.K.
body: After announcing that it will touch down in late founder Ozzy Osbourne ‘s hometown of Birmingham, U.K. next year, Ozzfest revealed that it will also hit the U.S. for the first time in nearly a decade in 2027. In an Instagram post on Monday (Sept. 21), the hard rock fest wrote, “Ozzfest will come to the U.K. and U.S. @theozzfest,” with the caption promising, “More Info Coming Soon!!! Where are you hoping Ozzfest 2027 will pop up?” At press time no additional information was available on the cities, dates or lineups for the reboot of the former touring hard rock festival. Ozzfest announced last month that the event would take place at Villa Park, Birmingham , the 42,000-capacity stadium that hosted Black Sabbath and Ozzy Osbourne ’s farewell show Back to the Beginning , which took place in July 2025; the event dates and lineup have not yet been shared for the Villa Park show. Ozzfest was cooked up by Ozzy’s wife and manager Sharon Osbourne in 1996 after she was unable to book Ozzy on the Lollapalooza festival. title: Google Messages is preparing its biggest search overhaul yet
summary: A sweeping redesign puts conversations, shared media, and results within easier reach.
body: TL;DR Google Messages is testing a search homepage that previews shared photos, videos, links, and places. Search could soon list every matching text and let you search within a specific conversation directly from the main page. Google is also testing swipeable media results and redesigned pages for in-chat searches, links, and places. Digging up an address, photo, or years-old texts in Google Messages can quickly turn into a search expedition. But Google appears to be working on a substantial search redesign that puts more of your shared content up front, lets you search within a specific chat from the main search page, and even shows every matching message without sending you hopping through conversations. title: الصحف الكتالونية تجلد مورينيو: أطنان من الصخب.. قليل من الكرة

title: فيديو: بيكيه يسخر من مورينيو وريال مدريد بطريقة مثيرة
summary: ماذا فعل؟
body: ماذا فعل؟ واصل ريال مدريد نتائجه المتراجعة بعد عامين دون تحقيق الألقاب، وتولي 3 مدربين مسؤولية الفريق، قبل أن يقرر فلورنتينو بيريز إعادة جوزيه مورينيو إلى القيادة الفنية، في محاولة لإعادة النادي إلى طريق المنافسة على البطولات. لكن بداية المدرب البرتغالي لم تأتِ بالشكل المنتظر، خاصة بعد الخسارة أمام أتلتيكو مدريد في ديربي العاصمة، لتتجدد الانتقادات حول مستوى الفريق تحت قيادة مورينيو. واستغل جيرارد بيكيه، مدافع برشلونة السابق والمشجع المعروف بانتمائه للنادي الكتالوني، الفرصة للسخرية من الغريم التقليدي، بعدما نشر مقطع فيديو عبر حسابه الرسمي على "تيك توك"، مستعيدًا ذكريات عام 2010. Pique mofandose de Mourinho 😭 pic.twitter.com/jARJfLdTJ4 — 𝘼𝙙𝙖𝙢. title: من السخرية إلى الهيمنة.. سيميوني يحول أتلتيكو إلى عقدة ريال مدريد

title: After trying this Walmart tablet, I’ll never buy an Android tablet from any other brand
summary: Onn isn't for everyone, but it might just be for you!
body: Credit: Andrew Grush / Android Authority Last spring, I wrote about how my family finally gave the iPad a try after more than a decade with Android tablets. At the time, I said we might still get newer Android tablets as backups eventually , since we have multiple family members. That happened earlier this summer, when we picked up the Onn Core 7-inch tablet, primarily for my youngest son. I was so impressed that my wife and I ended up with an Onn 11 Pro about a month later. While Onn tablets aren’t for everyone, I’ve found they’re a perfect fit for my family. In fact, I likely won’t buy an Android tablet from any other OEM going forward unless it can match Onn’s value.

title: Forgot your phone PIN? Google could look to the past to save you from a factory reset
summary: You could soon use your Google account credentials to recover your locked device, just like you could back in the day.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 includes code for a “Unlock with Google Account” feature, which would let users recover locked-out phones without performing a factory reset. Google previously allowed pattern unlock resets using Google account credentials until Android 4.4, but later removed the feature, forcing everyone locked out of their phone to factory reset. The unreleased feature appears to be optional, which would balance the needs of everyday consumers and security-conscious users. Google released Android 17 QPR2 Beta 5 last week, and we are digging into the release to see what the company has in store for us. We’ve now found clues of a new feature in the works that could soon let you unlock your Android phone with your linked Google account credentials if you ever forget your PIN or password, which could finally save users from the nuclear option of a factory reset when they are locked out of their devices. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. In fact, some reports say it’s one of the best-performing US carriers . body: I’ve tested dozens of wireless chargers and desk setups over the years, and most of them suffer from the same problem. They all try to shoehorn everything into a single hub. There’s little, if any, flexibility in placement, choice of charging options, or future upgradeability. Moreover, as a design enthusiast, I care a lot about how a particular piece of tech looks in my space, and most chargers just aren’t very pretty to look at. But looks are subjective. Anyway, the fact is that most charging stations expect you to conform to a fixed layout for your phone, earbuds, and smartwatch . title: This simple Duolingo trick brings back hearts and gets rid of the annoying ads

body: Credit: Matt Horne / Android Authority Even as one of the last remaining Duolingo holdouts on the team, I can see how much worse Duolingo has become in recent years. The once-motivating gamification certainly appears to have been kicked up a few notches, and it’s the free users who’ve had it much worse. On the free plan, you’re bombarded with adverts for Super Duolingo and third-party games that you can’t skip for several seconds. Even worse, the heart system that allowed you to keep practicing until you made five mistakes was replaced by an energy bar that runs down even if you’re nailing the answers. That’s why I was excited to learn about a very simple trick that returns you to a simpler version of Duolingo — one with the hearts system, no ads at all, fewer clicks between lessons, and less gamification.

But not all the accessories in Google’s charging ecosystem are as good — and I’m pointing fingers squarely at the PixelSnap charger (). While MagSafe undoubtedly has some conveniences for case accessories, it’s proven to be a significant downgrade in terms of what actually matters — charging times. body: You hear horror stories of people unwittingly incurring monstrous mobile bills when roaming abroad. Just recently, one Reddit user was horrified to find that AT&T had clobbered them with a $53k charge , after an eight-day European trip they expected to run them about $100 in roaming fees. You tend to feel sorry for these people, while also having lingering thoughts that they’ve been dealt a very tough life lesson. Thankfully, my own roaming-fee surprise involved considerably fewer zeroes. I only incurred about $20 in roaming charges, so not a big hit, but what bothered me was that I’d done everything right to avoid using mobile data . At least, I thought I had. You might be thinking I’m just as culpable, and maybe lucky I wasn’t charged more. I can assure you that wasn’t the case. I hadn’t forgotten to switch something over after landing, and this wasn’t a travel eSIM taking a few seconds to wake up. In fact, I wasn’t trying to use data at all. title: I used Immich for years, but this self-hosted Google Photos alternative is even better

body: I’ve had Immich running on my home server for the past three years. It’s a self-hosting essential for me as I try to offload as much of my backups and services from the cloud as possible. It’s where I keep the photos from my SLR, where my phone backs up photos automatically, and where I can search through years of images without handing everything over to Google. For a self-hosted alternative to Google Photos , there’s little doubt that Immich is the go-to for most. But as good as Immich is, as an enthusiast, I was bound to run into limitations. Immich is great at managing individual photo libraries, but it isn’t always great at managing a family’s photo library. If you’re trying to share a portion of your library, Immich makes it extremely hard. And you can absolutely forget about sharing certain aspects of the library, like metadata.

title: Gemini’s rough patch with smart home controls has spread to Android Auto
summary: One Gemini smart home bug gets fixed, another pops up.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Some Android Auto users say Gemini has suddenly stopped controlling their smart home devices. The issue follows recent Gemini smart home control problems on Wear OS, which Google said it had fixed. It’s not clear what’s causing the Android Auto problem — we’ve reached out to Google for comment. Gemini has had a rough couple of weeks with smart home controls. Wear OS users recently reported that Gemini would claim it had controlled lights, AC units, and other devices when nothing actually happened , before Google said that the issue had been fixed . It isn’t clear if it’s related, but some Android Auto users are now finding that Gemini suddenly refuses to control their smart home devices, even though those same commands worked previously. In a post on the r/AndroidAuto subreddit earlier today, one user says that Gemini has stopped executing commands such as turning on the AC. Instead, it now responds that it “cannot control smart home devices through Google Maps while driving.” The poster says the feature had been working for months before this change.

title: Android 17 QPR1 fixes a major headache for enthusiasts
summary: No more turning developer options off to check your bank account.
body: TL;DR Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Pixel phones now. The update no longer allows third-party apps to see whether you have developer settings or USB debugging active. This should make life easier for anyone who tinkers with Android’s more advanced settings. Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out now to Pixel phones going back to the Pixel 6. The update brings a number of changes, including UI tweaks, the option to include photo location metadata in images shared through Android’s media picker, and more. As spotted by a user on X, QPR1 also quietly fixes an issue that’s been a thorn in the side of Android enthusiasts for years. As developer Sameera Wijerahna points out in a post on X , Android 17 QPR1 no longer lets third-party apps see the state of developer options or debugging settings. This could be a big deal for developers or anyone else who likes to tinker with their Android devices — prior to the change, some apps wouldn’t open on devices with certain settings active.
